etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Elongation of おい.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Clipping of サボタージュ (sabotāju, “idling, truancy”) + る (-ru, verb-forming suffix), the former from French sabotage.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English space.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English set.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English data.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English fight. Compare the semantics of Korean 파이팅 (paiting), 화이팅 (hwaiting).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese compound 一切 (MC 'jit tshejH). Compare modern Mandarin 一切 (yīqiè).
The goon reading, so likely the earlier import.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese compound 一切 (MC 'jit tshet). The kan'on reading, so likely the later import.
Appears to be less common than the issai reading.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 一(ひと) (hito, “one”) + 切(き)り (kiri, “cut, cutting”, 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 切(き)る (kiru, “to cut”)).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 一(ひと) (hito, “one”) + 切(き)れ (kire, “cut, cutting”, the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 切(き)れる (kireru, “to be cut apart, to be broken apart”)).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese 主 (MC tsyuX).
The kan'on pronunciation, so likely a later borrowing.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese 云云 (MC hjun hjun). The un changes to nun as an instance of renjō (連(れん)声(じょう)).
First cited to 1110.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From classical yodan(四段活用) verb 伴(ともな)ふ (tomonafu), formed from とも (tomo, “companion”) + なふ (nafu, verb-forming suffix).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 先天(せんてん) (senten, “congenital”) + 的(てき) (-teki, “-like”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 内 (“inside”) + 蔵 (“to store”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 内 (“inside”) + 蔵 (“storehouse”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 名 (na) + 付ける (tsukeru). The tsukeru changes to zukeru as an instance of rendaku (連濁)..

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/teibau/ → /teibɔː/ → /teiboː/
From Middle Chinese compound 堤防 (dei? bjang, literally “dike, embankment + dike”). Compare modern Cantonese reading tai⁴ fong⁴.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
尊 (tōto, tatto, stem of 尊い (tōtoi, tattoi, “noble, exalted, sacred”)) + ぶ (-bu, “to act like”)
The ぶ (-bu) suffix usually conjugated with the upper bigrade pattern (上二段活用 (kami nidan katsuyō)), and 尊ぶ conjugated this way in Old Japanese. Since the Heian period, 尊ぶ shifted to conjugate using the classical yodan pattern, the precursor to the modern godan conjugation (五段活用 (godan katsuyō)).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 手(て) (te, “means”) + 順(じゅん) (-jun, “order”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 手(て) (te, “hand”) + の (no, “-'s”, genitive particle) + 平(ひら) (hira, “flat”). Compare English flat of one's hand.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 手(た) (ta-, “hand”) + な (na, “-'s”, archaic) + 裏(うら) (ura, “backside, hidden side”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 手(た) (ta-, “hand”) + な (na, “-'s”, archaic) + 心(こころ) (kokoro, “heart; inside”, rendaku form 心(ごころ) (gokoro)).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 掌 (MC tsyangX).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *suru. Cognate with Proto-Ryukyuan *suri.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Cognate with 霞(かす)む (kasumu, “to grow hazy, to become blurry”), which see for further cognates. Compare also 擦(す)る (suru, “to rub”) above.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Possibly a compound of こ (ko) + 擦(す)る (suru, “to rub”). The ko element might be 粉(こ) (ko, “powder, flour”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Unknown. A {{glossary|surface analysis suggests a compound with the second element being 擦(す)る (suru, “to rub”).
First cited to a text from c. 1809-1813.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Derived from 水 (mi, “water”, combining form); な (na, Old Japanese possessive particle); 元, 本 (moto, “origin, source”).
Vovin believes that the na in the initial mina- element is not a genitive particle, but rather actually meant "water", contending that the mi was instead the honorific prefix 御 (mi-). See also 港 (minato, “sluice; port”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 源 (MC ngjwon).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese compound 激勵 (MC kek ljejH).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 無駄 (“futility, waste”) + 遣い (“use, usage”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 真っ (ma'-, “truly”) + 二つ (futatsu, “two parts”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Shift from 素気(すげ)ない (sugenai)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese, attested in the Kakyō Hyōshiki of 772 with the phonetic spelling 倶基. In turn, from Proto-Japonic *kukuy.
This word has an alternating form くく (kuku) which only occurs in compounds. For the reason of this vowel alternation, see WT:AJPX#Standalone forms and combining forms.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 連 is a daiyōji replacing 聯.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese. Ultimate roots uncertain. May be cognate with 病む (yamu, “to be ill”), 止む (yamu, “to stop, to quit”), 黄泉 (yomi, “land of the dead”).
Reconstructed as deriving ultimately from Proto-Japonic *yamui.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 闇 (MC 'omH, “dark”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From 帰(かえ)り (kaeri, 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 帰(かえ)る (kaeru, “to return, to go home”).) + 見(み)る (miru, “to look, to watch, to take care”).
The み (mi) is written as an okurigana to indicate the reading of 顧.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese.
Likely cognate with Korean 삼 (sam, “hemp”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/wo/ → /o/
From Old Japanese 麻 (wo).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Possibly from an altered pronunciation of asa.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 麻 (MC mae, “hemp”).
